terms.gloss: to make a harsh, shrill sound: screech, hiss, creak, whiz
evidence: Ov. F. 6.140: strīgēs, of screech owls (Lewis & Short)
Plin. NH 29.138: gryllus, of a cricket (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Also strīdō, strīdere, both forms equally in use, Lewis & Short. Traupman uses it for an ape’s chatter, an eagle’s or falcon’s screech and a locust’s chirp. The noun is strīdor, strīdōris m.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
